subject: Post-call: translating burst into steady capacity — FlowShip next steps
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@flowship.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: translating burst into steady capacity — FlowShip next steps

Hi Samira — thanks again for the productive call earlier. Quick written recap so we have a shared place to iterate and capture the numbers we discussed. I’ve attached the call notes (call-notes-20270630.pdf) and flagged the ask list below.

Call takeaways (short):
- Target SLOs: p95 generation latency target = 200 ms (hard for full-stream cases), target for short single-turn requests = 100 ms p95.
- Observed burst behavior (what you reported): short bursts of high concurrency during checkout flows and live-chat escalations. Peak bursts reported as ~28k tokens/sec during 60–120s windows.
- Baseline/steady: ~4k tokens/sec across business hours.
- Avg tokens per request: ~85–110 tokens (range varies by template).
- Streaming: ~40–60 concurrent streaming sessions during peak bursts; streaming is critical for the chat UX.

Asks / what we need from FlowShip to produce a preliminary sizing:
1) 3–7 day traffic export with per-request timestamps, tokens/request, whether streaming was used, and a session id (CSV/Parquet).
2) Clarify the largest contiguous peak window you care about (we heard 60–120s; confirm if you need sizing for 30m sustained peaks or just the short spikes).
3) Any hard constraints for fallback behavior (e.g., max degrading latency or model quality acceptable).

Preliminary notes from our side (will formalize after we see the traffic sample):
- Translating tokens/sec -> QPS: with 90 tokens/avg we’re looking at ~310 QPS for the 28k tokens/sec burst.
- Streaming concurrency of ~50 during peak suggests we should consider both reserved concurrency and prewarmed KV-serving capacity.
- Caching/prefix reuse can reduce token compute by ~15–25% for templated requests — worth instrumenting.

Next steps / proposed schedule:
- Samira to share the 3-day sample link by EOD Friday (thanks!)
- Redwood (Ben + Marissa) to turn around a first-draft sizing and recommended Dedicated pool config within 48 hours of receiving the sample.
- Follow-up sync to review sizing and tradeoffs (30 min).

Thanks — I’ll coordinate the follow-up once the export is in.

—
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Platform Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: translating burst into steady capacity — FlowShip next steps

Thanks Aisha, and appreciated the clear recap. Couple clarifications and answers to your asks below — we’ll push the export to the shared Drive link you provided (Drive link below) by Friday noon.

Clarifications / numbers from our side:
- Peak burst: confirmed ~28,000 tokens/sec but that was measured during a 90–110s checkout surge. We do see rarer events where multiple campaigns overlap and the window can extend to 7–10 minutes, though those aren’t the norm.
- Baseline steady: 3.5k–4.5k tokens/sec (typical weekday hours).
- Avg tokens/request: we ran a quick sample, median is 92 tokens, 75th percentile is ~160 (some long form responses).
- Streaming: concurrency approx 50 at peak; most streaming sessions are ~8–12s of active token generation.

We can provide the 3-day parquet export at: https://drive.google.com/flowship/sample-3day-parquet (will include columns: timestamp, request_id, tokens, streaming_bool, session_id).

Fallback: if latency degrades we can accept a degraded-bandwidth fallback for <10% of requests during extreme peaks (prefer shorter responses vs total dropped responses).

Let us know if you need schema details for the parquet — happy to chat.

—
Samira Khan
Head of Platform Integrations
FlowShip

Great — thanks Samira. When we get the parquet we’ll run the traffic-tagger and return a short annotated histogram (tokens per request, streaming fraction, peak window length).

Preliminary mapping (high level) — will validate against actual export:
- 28k tokens/sec burst -> ~310–370 QPS (90–75 tokens/request range).
- For streaming-heavy requests we plan to size for peak concurrent streaming >= 60 to provide headroom (50 reported peak + buffer).
- If FlowShip prefers to limit reserved GPUs, we can propose a hybrid: small Dedicated pool sized for steady-state + short-lived burst lanes on hosted capacity with automated fallback routing.

Attached is a first-pass workbook (proposed-sizing-v1.xlsx) with the assumptions used. Ben / Marissa — once you’ve had a first look, can you validate the GPU-equivalent calc and recommend a starting Dedicated pool (GPU type and count) we should propose to Samira?

Next: we’ll wait for the parquet and then propose the recommended Dedicated config within 48 hours.

Thanks — I’ll schedule the 30-min review for Monday morning (tentative).

—
Aisha Rahman
Account Executive, Platform Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: rough sizing calc (do not forward)

Internal note before we lock the external recommendation — quick back-of-envelope using A100-equivalent token throughput: 
- Assumptions: 1 A100-equiv can sustain ~8k tokens/sec for our gen model (with quantization and batching).
- For 28k tokens/sec burst -> ~3.5 A100-equiv sustained during peak. Put another way: 4x A100-equiv gives headroom for 90–120s peaks.
- Steady baseline 4k tokens/sec -> 0.5 A100-equiv (so 1 GPU could cover steady with margin).
- Streaming concurrency: streaming sessions increase memory/kv pressure; recommend prewarmed lane (1 GPU) dedicated to streaming kernel paths in addition to compute pool.

Recommendation options to present to FlowShip:
1) Conservative (preferred for critical UX): Dedicated pool = 4 x A100-equiv + 1 prewarmed streaming GPU (could be a smaller T4 for cost).
2) Hybrid (cost-optimized): Dedicated pool = 1 x A100-equiv for steady + hosted-burst on Redwood Hosted with automated routing (estimated risk: tail latency bump during simultaneous campaigns).

Marissa / Ben — any quick adjustments before I send the formal proposal? I’ll fold in your GPU-type preferences and cost delta into the workbook.

—
Aisha
Account Executive, Platform Sales
Redwood Inference
